title: Magnons reveal topology and dynamics of a skyrmion crystal
authors: Raphael Ayache, Nilotpal Chakraborty, Manabendra Kuiri, Quentin Benichou, Antonio Lacerda-Santos, Lilian Seyve, Himadri Chakraborti, Leo Pugliese, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Cosimo Gorini, Roderich Moessner, Benoit Doucot, Preden Roulleau
abstract: Although individual skyrmions are topologically protected objects, their cooperative crystalline order is fragile, easily disrupted by thermal fluctuations or other external perturbations. Probing the internal dynamics of such a crystal is both compelling and challenging, as its intricate and delicate spin texture must remain stable during measurement. Here, we engineer a nanoscale graphene junction hosting a skyrmion Wigner crystal, embedded between magnon emitters and detectors. The skyrmion crystal geometry leaves a striking imprint on magnon transport: as the gate voltage is varied, near-periodic windows of sharp fluctuations in magnon count are detected across the entire sample. We develop an interpretation that this results from skyrmions being added one by one to a quasi-one-dimensional array. Each burst of the fluctuations thus corresponds to the entry of an additional skyrmion, during which the lattice stiffness reduces. The impinging magnons induce and act as a probe of non-equilibrium collective dynamics of the crystal. These results establish a real-space probe of topological spin textures in quantum Hall-type insulating ground states via magnon transport and open opportunities to explore correlated, topologically ordered phases in moire and multilayer graphene systems.
summary: Researchers used magnon transport measurements on a graphene junction hosting a skyrmion Wigner crystal to study its internal dynamics. By monitoring sharp, periodic fluctuations in the magnon signal as the gate voltage was tuned, they provided direct evidence that individual skyrmions are added sequentially to the crystal lattice. This establishes magnons as a powerful real-space probe for correlated, topologically ordered phases.
main_problem: The primary challenge is probing the internal dynamics and topology of a skyrmion crystal, whose cooperative crystalline order is inherently fragile.
main_result: The detection of near-periodic fluctuations in magnon count confirms that individual skyrmions are added sequentially to the quasi-1D array, providing real-space insight into the lattice stiffness reduction during this process.
method: The study uses non-local magnon transport measurements ($	ext{dV}_{	ext{NL},i}/	ext{dI}$) in a nanoscale graphene junction, acting as a sensitive probe for topological spin textures.
model_or_system: The system is a nanoscale graphene junction hosting a skyrmion Wigner crystal within the Quantum Hall Effect regime. The physics involves interacting electrons forming topologically protected skyrmions stabilized by Coulomb interaction.
key_observables: Near-periodic windows of sharp fluctuations in magnon count, and the non-local signal onset above the Zeeman energy ($E_Z$).
important_parameters:
Gate voltage (controlling filling factor $
u$), bias voltage ($V_{ds}$), and the excess charge ($\epsilon$) driving skyrmion formation.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the non-local response is dominated by bulk magnons propagating across the sample, and that the observed fluctuations correspond to discrete single-skyrmion additions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup (graphene junction with gates), show the magnon signal onset at $E_Z$ vs. bias voltage, and display $	ext{dV}_{	ext{NL},i}/	ext{dI}$ dependence on gate voltages to highlight the fluctuation regimes.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical platform (graphene QHE junction), details the measurement technique using non-local magnon transport, presents evidence for skyrmion crystallization via voltage tuning, and interprets the resulting periodic fluctuations as single-skyrmion addition events.
why_interesting: This work provides an experimental realization of probing collective dynamics in a topologically ordered state (the skyrmion crystal) using quasiparticle excitations (magnons), which is highly relevant to understanding correlated electron behavior beyond simple band theory.

FIG. 2. Magnon response probing the real-space topology of a skyrmion crystal. a,b, Schematics of the skyrmion crystal junction. Upon doping the lowest Landau level beyond ν = 1, the added charge is accommodated by topological spin textures (skyrmions) (a). Slightly away from ν = 1, these skyrmions crystallize into a topological Wigner crystal confined within the junction (b). Magnons emitted from a single injector (Em2) are scattered by the crystal and detected through the nonlocal response. c, Hall conductance as a function of the left-gate voltage. The light-blue region, slightly away from ν = 1, marks the gate-voltage window where sharp fluctuations in the nonlocal signal are observed....
